correctness.rationale: For every nondegenerate ideal quadrilateral, normalize to ordered vertices (0,1,lambda,infinity). Exact perpendicular-geodesic distance gives the three competing quantities y,lambda/y,(lambda+y^2)/((lambda-1)y). Their normalized minimum is invariant under x<->1/x, has a unique interior switch exactly for lambda>3, and peaks at sqrt(lambda) or sqrt(lambda/(lambda-2)). Möbius half-turn exchanges opposite sides; relabeling changes lambda to lambda/(lambda-1). The larger parameter kappa dominates the smaller, proving a globally sharp H(kappa), unique nonregular maximum kappa=3, regular-square local minimum and one-to-two farthest-point transition. The provided independent point-to-point numerical geometry check passes 5335 comparisons; the infinite-family proof is fully analytic.

value.rationale: Side slimness is a natural metric invariant of geodesic polygons, motivated independently of the computation. The theorem determines it across every ideal four-gon shape, giving a sharp universal nonregular extremizer and exact location/contact bifurcation. These conclusions are not just a parameter substitution or textbook calculation of one square: they characterize an entire moduli space, including an unexpected nonregular maximizer and a degenerating triangle limit.
